text:
New Jersey arrives with the better underlying numbers. At five on five the Devils have taken 62% of the expected goals, creating 3.67 per 60 while allowing 2.72. Washington sits at 50% (3.50 for, 3.85 against). The Devils have an even goal difference despite being plus 6.7 in expected goals, and their finishing (minus 3.0) and goaltending (minus 3.8 saved above expected) have cost them. Both teams are 3-2-0 in their last five, but New Jersey has 57% of the expected goals in that stretch to Washington's 50%. The model has it close, 3.33 to 3.07 for the Devils.

Special teams could matter. Washington takes 5.0 penalties a game and its penalty kill allows 0.94 expected goals a game, against 0.64 for New Jersey. The Devils' power play generates 0.63 a game to Washington's 0.55. The goalie matchup is the one clear edge for the Capitals. Logan Thompson (projected) is at plus 4.07 goals saved above expected in five starts after plus 28.16 across 58 games last season. Jake Allen (projected) is at minus 1.32 in four starts, after plus 5.39 in 37 games last year. Both teams are missing a forward to illness, Washington's Pierre-Luc Dubois and New Jersey's Luke Evangelista, with estimated returns of Oct 20.

Jack Hughes is the player to watch. He carries a five-game point streak and has a 36% chance to score and 70% to record a point. Jesper Bratt has nine points in four games against Washington, and Alex Tuch leads the Capitals at 36% to score. Declan Chisholm also returns to Washington for the first time since leaving the Capitals, though the model doesn't price that.
